page_title: There’s no speed limit | Derek Sivers

summary.title: There's no speed limit
summary.one_liner: A personal story of how a music teacher, Kimo Williams, compressed two years of Berklee College harmony and arranging into a few lessons, showing that the standard pace is optional.
takeaways: A single teacher with high expectations can change a student's trajectory in only a few lessons.
Jazz harmony concepts like the tri-tone and flat-7 substitution can be taught through rapid quizzing.
Students can test out of college requirements and self-study courses to finish degrees faster, as Sivers did (graduating in two and a half years).
The author's core lesson: the system is designed so driven people can keep up, and there is no speed limit on learning.
summary.summary: Derek Sivers recounts how, at seventeen, he took a few lessons from studio owner and Berklee alumnus Kimo Williams before starting at Berklee College of Music. Williams drilled him on jazz harmony, covering a full semester in the first lesson and six semesters across five lessons. Sivers tested out of those requirements, self-studied the remaining courses, and passed the final exams, graduating in two and a half years. The piece is a personal essay rather than a how-to, and it closes with Sivers' reflection that high expectations removed his sense of a speed limit.
